title: Creating the database and saving
summary: EnsureCreated against migrations, and the add, query, change, save loop.

steps.title: EnsureCreated and migrations
body: Something has to create the tables. EF Core offers two ways:

**`db.Database.EnsureCreated()`** looks at your model and, if the database does not exist, creates it with every table. If it already exists, it does nothing, *even if your classes changed since*. It returns `true` when it created something.

**Migrations** record each change to your model as a small C# file (`AddBooks`, `AddAuthorToBooks`, ...) and apply them in order, so an existing database with real data is *altered*, not recreated. You create them with the `dotnet ef` command-line tool (module 6).
| Good for | demos, tests, throwaway data | any database whose data you keep |
| Classes change later | ignored | applied as `ALTER TABLE` and friends |
| History | none | one file per change, in source control |
Never mix them on one database: a database made by `EnsureCreated` has no migration history, so migrations cannot be applied to it later.
In this course every program starts in an empty folder, so `EnsureCreated` is all we need until module 6.

steps.prompt: Your app is in production with real customer data. You add a `Phone` property to `Customer`. What should create the new column?
options: A migration, applied to the existing database
Nothing: EF Core adds columns automatically on the next query
steps.explain: `EnsureCreated` never alters an existing database, and deleting it loses the data. Migrations exist exactly for evolving a database that holds data you keep.
The first call creates the database (`True`). The second finds it already there (`False`). `EnsureDeleted` deletes it and returns `True`, so the last `EnsureCreated` creates it again.

steps.title: Change and save
body: The context remembers every entity it gave you. This is **change tracking**: change a property and call `SaveChanges`, and EF Core works out the `UPDATE` itself.
`SaveChanges` returns the number of rows it wrote, and it sends all pending changes in one transaction: either all of them succeed or none do.

steps.prompt: Arrange the lines into a program that adds a book, saves it, then fixes its year and saves again.
lines: var book = new Book { Title = "Dune", Year = 1956 };
steps.explain: The book must be added and saved before there is a row to update. The second `SaveChanges` sees the changed `Year` and sends an `UPDATE`.

code: db.Books.AddRange(new Book { Title = "A", Year = 2000 }, new Book { Title = "B", Year = 2001 }, new Book { Title = "C", Year = 2002 });
steps.explain: Three inserts, then one update plus one delete (2 rows). Ordered by year, B (1999) now comes before A (2000), and C is gone.

steps.prompt: Complete the method that renames a book. It returns `false` when there is no book with that id.
code: bool Rename(LibraryDb db, int id, string title)
steps.explain: `FirstOrDefault` gives `null` when nothing matches (`Single` would throw). Changing the tracked entity and calling `SaveChanges` is all it takes to update it.

steps.title: A reading list
prompt: The tests give you a `LibraryDb` with a `Books` table (`Id`, `Title`, `Year`, and a `bool Read`). Write three methods:
- `int AddBook(LibraryDb db, string title, int year)` adds an unread book, saves, and returns its new `Id`.
- `bool MarkRead(LibraryDb db, int id)` marks that book as read and saves. Returns `false` if there is no such book.
- `List<string> Unread(LibraryDb db)` returns the titles of unread books, oldest first.
starter: int AddBook(LibraryDb db, string title, int year)
solution: int AddBook(LibraryDb db, string title, int year)
var book = new Book { Title = title, Year = year };
template: Dojo.Eq("AddBook returns the generated ids", new List<int> { 1, 2, 3 }, new List<int> { dojoDune, dojoEmma, dojoHobbit });
Dojo.Eq("the books were saved (seen from a new context)", 3, dojoDb.Books.Count());
Dojo.Eq("Unread lists all three, oldest first", new List<string> { "Emma", "The Hobbit", "Dune" }, Unread(dojoDb));
Dojo.Eq("MarkRead(2) returns true", true, MarkRead(dojoDb, dojoEmma));
Dojo.Eq("MarkRead saved the change", true, dojoDb.Books.Single(b => b.Id == dojoEmma).Read);
Dojo.Eq("Unread leaves out read books", new List<string> { "The Hobbit", "Dune" }, Unread(dojoDb));
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=reading.db");
hints: After `SaveChanges`, the new object's `Id` holds the generated key.
`db.Books.Find(id)` looks a row up by primary key and returns `null` when there is none.
